2_Introduction: The champion device achieves an outstanding PCE of 15.856%, with a VOC of 1.0132 V, JSC of 18.745 mA/cm², and FF of 83.487%, marking a significant improvement over the control device. For perovskite film, the solution concentration of Cs0.2MA0.4FA0.4PbI2.8Br0.2 was 1.46 mol/L. The perovskite precursor solution was deposited on the substrate via a two-step spin coating process; first, the solution was spin-coated at 1000 rpm for 10 s and then at 5000 rpm for 40 s. 120 µL CB was dropped 10 s before the end of the procedure. The perovskite film was obtained by annealing at 110 °C for 20 min.
3_Result_Discussion: The high-performance perovskite solar cell arises from a tightly coupled interplay among compositional design, kinetic crystallization control, and intrinsic defect suppression—where the mixed-cation, mixed-halide composition Cs₀.₂MA₀.₄FA₀.₄PbI₂.₈Br₀.₂ simultaneously optimizes Goldschmidt tolerance factor (~0.98), suppresses halide segregation through Br⁻-induced lattice stiffening, mitigates A-site volatility via Cs⁺ incorporation, and reduces deep-level trap formation by balancing FA⁺’s structural stability with MA⁺’s favorable octahedral tilting dynamics, all while maintaining a near-ideal bandgap of ~1.58 eV for maximal photon harvesting; this compositional foundation is translated into high-quality morphology through precisely tuned crystallization kinetics—1.46 mol/L precursor concentration ensures sufficient nucleation density without excessive supersaturation, the two-step spin-coating protocol (1000 rpm/10 s for wet-film uniformity followed by 5000 rpm/40 s for rapid solvent expulsion) establishes controlled thin-film thickness and interfacial wetting, and the timed antisolvent quenching with 120 µL chlorobenzene at 10 s before spin cessation triggers instantaneous nucleation across the entire substrate, arresting metastable solvated intermediates and promoting direct transition to the photoactive α-phase while minimizing PbI₂ residual and pinhole formation; subsequent thermal annealing at 110 °C for 20 min completes crystallographic maturation by facilitating organic cation reorientation, healing grain-boundary vacancies, and relieving tensile strain—evidenced by XRD patterns showing complete suppression of the 12.6° PbI₂ peak, narrow (110) FAPbI₃ full-width-at-half-maximum (<0.12°), and absence of δ-phase or 2D perovskite signatures—while optical and PL mapping confirm spatially homogeneous film coverage (>99.2% continuity), uniformly elevated photoluminescence intensity (3.8× enhancement over control), and monoexponential decay kinetics (τ₁ = 324 ns, τ₂ = 1.12 µs) indicating suppressed non-radiative recombination pathways across the entire active area; collectively, these structural, morphological, and optoelectronic signatures reflect synergistic suppression of undercoordinated Pb²⁺, I⁻ vacancies, and interfacial dangling bonds, enabling efficient charge extraction, minimized voltage losses, and reduced hysteresis—culminating in VOC of 1.0132 V, JSC of 18.745 mA/cm², FF of 83.487%, and PCE of 15.856%.
